A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and provide readable main text, Appendices A–I, Figures 1–9, and Tables 1–23. Text reflow does not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: Sections 5–6 and the appendices report original neural-network experiments on OOD detection and transfer, component ablations, representation analyses, and computational efficiency.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experimental results, including the main comparisons and detailed appendix evaluations.

M1.justification: The entropy-regularized encoder, frozen two-layer simplex ETF projector, normalization choices, classification objective, and task-specific use of representations remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendix A.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet-100, ImageNet-10 diagnostic experiments, and the same eight OOD image datasets. The added continual-learning and dataset-bias discussion introduces no evaluated task or scenario.

E2.justification: The standard DNN baselines, NECO comparisons in Tables 5 and 22, and component comparison methods retain the same membership. Newly cited continual-learning methods are not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: Training schedules, dataset splits, preprocessing, model configurations, linear probing, and evaluation metrics match across Section 5 and Appendices A–C. No new evaluation protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: The entropy, projector, classifier, normalization, loss-function, and optimizer ablations are retained. UMAP visualizations, energy distributions, layerwise correlations, and training-dynamics analyses also remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Point estimates, cross-dataset averaging, and Pearson-correlation reporting are unchanged. Neither version specifies repeated-run or seed counts, uncertainty intervals, or significance testing.

E6.justification: Tables 1–23 and the experimental figures retain their results. For example, Table 2 reports VGG17+Ours transfer error of 41.85% and detection error of 65.10% in both versions. The new continual-learning discussion supplies interpretations rather than additional measured outcomes.

T1.justification: Propositions 4.1 and E.1, the entropy proof, loss derivation, simplex ETF formula, and neural-collapse metric definitions are unchanged. Statements moving across page boundaries are retained mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same detection–transfer trade-off and layer-specific neural-collapse control claims. The introduction rephrases the existing novelty assertion without changing its substantive scope.

C2.justification: Section 7 adds implications for biased datasets and a continual-learning argument linking controlled neural collapse to knowledge preservation, improving representations over time, and reduced replay needs. V2 treated continual learning as a future extension; these additional interpretations receive no corresponding experimental evaluation.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, and resource information are retained. V3 moves and repeats the existing code-site disclosure in the abstract and Appendix A; the destination is identical to v2's introduction footnote.

R1.justification: V3 adds nine references concerning continual-learning metrics, replay, efficiency, and bias mitigation, expanding the positioning in Sections 2.2 and 7. These include Hayes et al. (2018, 2019), Harun et al. (2023a–c), and Shrestha et al. (2022a,b); the central NC/OOD positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: There are localized prose edits, an expanded discussion with three topical headings, and relocation of the code disclosure. The overall section sequence and most scientific exposition are retained.

P2.justification: Table 1 corrects 'Encover' to 'Encoder', while Figure 4 and Table 7 receive caption wording edits. Text and some displays shift through reflow, including the conclusion moving to page 10; figure contents and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V3 adds useful context and clearer discussion headings, but Section 7 now presents knowledge preservation and representations improving over time as demonstrated results, then suggests reduced replay needs. V2 framed continual learning as future work. Neither PDF reports sequential-learning, forgetting, or replay evaluations supporting these assertions. This overextension of unchanged evidence modestly weakens interpretive rigor despite the contextual and presentation benefits.
